summary.title: Learn X in Y minutes: Learn C
summary.one_liner: A fast, code-heavy tour of C covering comments, types, arrays, operators, control flow, pointers, manual memory management with malloc/free, and functions.
keywords: c functions and call by reference
takeaways: C has no Boolean type; 0 is false and any other value is true, and comparisons yield 0 or 1.
Arrays decay to pointers when passed to functions, so their size must be passed separately.
Heap memory from malloc/calloc/realloc must be checked and freed manually to avoid leaks.
Floating-point values are IEEE 754 and need epsilon-based comparisons; integer division and modulo with negatives behave specially.
Signed bit shifts and out-of-range shifts are undefined behavior, so care is needed.
summary.summary: This is a quick-reference tutorial in the 'Learn X in Y minutes' series that teaches C through commented, runnable-style code snippets. It walks through comments, preprocessor directives and headers, function prototypes, main and command-line arguments, primitive types and sizeof, arrays and strings, operators (including floating-point and bitwise pitfalls), control flow including goto, typecasting, pointers and dynamic memory, and functions with pass-by-value versus pointer parameters. Each example shows expected output inline, and notes call out undefined behavior and common mistakes.
